correctness.rationale: For every odd n=2k+1>=3, transitive subtournaments are precisely subsets of forward consecutive blocks, identified with a good circular-arc nerve and hence S1. Each 4-vertex subset containing a directed triangle has exactly two such triangles, since vertex in/out neighborhoods are transitive, so F1 attaches exactly C_n cyclic 2-simplices. The integral short-edge winding cocycle evaluates to 1 on every attaching loop. Thus F1 is a wedge of C_n-1 S2 and H2 identifies with the dihedral signed augmentation kernel. F2 contains the full 3-skeleton of the simplex, killing H1 and H2 for all higher thresholds. Finite exact enumerations over n=3,5,7,9,11 independently corroborate counts, winding and mod-two Betti numbers; no infinite conclusion relies on these finite checks.

value.rationale: The 3-cycle directionality filtration is a published natural topological invariant of tournaments. For every odd cyclic tournament, the result completely determines its degree-one and degree-two integral persistence (one bar [0,1) and C_n-1 bars [1,2)), the exact stage-one homotopy and the full signed dihedral lattice. The feedback-triangle count grows cubically, and the theorem explains a structural dimension shift rather than recomputing an arbitrary isolated Betti number. Higher persistence and unrelated tournament families are explicitly excluded.
